title: Janapada of Anga
capsule: Anga was one of the sixteen mahājanapadas of ancient India, occupying the lower Gangetic plain in the region of modern Bhagalpur and Munger districts of Bihar, with its capital at Campā on the Ganga-Champa confluence. It is mentioned in the Atharva Veda and the Mahābhārata as a distinct kingdom renowned for its wealth from river trade; the epic tradition records it as the kingdom ruled by Karṇa, and Jain texts note connections to the Tirthankara tradition in the region. Anga was conquered by Magadha under King Bimbisāra (r. c. 543–492 BCE), who absorbed it as a province and ended its independent existence before the attested end date of c. 500 BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Anga's general location in eastern Bihar is consistent across textual sources, but precise borders are inferred from literary geography rather than archaeological demarcation and carry substantial uncertainty.
